evidence: src/controllers/cardsController.ts: create, activate, getStatement, blockCard, unblockCard and createVirtual each call a single cardServices method and send a response.
src/controllers/paymentsController.ts: buyOnPointOfSale and buyOnline delegate to paymentServices.insertPayment and paymentServices.insertOnlinePayment, with no business logic in the controller.
src/controllers/rechargeController.ts: recharge delegates to rechargeService.recharge(cardId, amount) and returns 200.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three controllers do the same job. Each is a thin Express handler that reads req.body or req.params, calls one method on a business-layer service, and sends a status or payload. None holds business rules, touches persistence, or skips its service. No rule or invariant is duplicated across the files. Small differences, such as typed body destructuring only in paymentsController and parseInt on cardId only in getStatement, don't split the unit into separate concerns. The payment body interfaces are exported from paymentsController and used by src/schemas and src/services. That is an import-direction and placement matter, which is out of scope, and it doesn't make the controller files incoherent.
